counterfactual: On 30 October 2026 the Court of Appeal dismissed Patterson's conviction appeal. It granted leave on two grounds but rejected them, and rejected all seven grounds overall. On the hotel issue, McLeish said there was "nothing beyond speculation" to set against the jury keeper's assurance that there had been no contact. The court then dismissed the DPP's sentence appeal and left the life sentence with a 33-year non-parole period in place, so she remains eligible for parole around 2056. The judges called the offending "callous and deliberate" and accepted that it fell within the worst category of murder. But they found that Justice Beale had not erred in weighing her onerous, near-solitary custody, and that the sentence was "stern but within the range reasonably open". They noted that a minimum term of 33 years meant she would be in her eighties before she could be considered for release, if she were ever released at all. It remained among the longest non-parole periods imposed on a woman in Victorian legal history. Patterson, 52, watched by video link from the Dame Phyllis Frost Centre. Her only remaining avenue is a special leave application to the High Court of Australia, due within 28 days.

C3S reported that September 2026 was the warmest September on record globally, narrowly surpassing September 2023. Global average surface air temperature was 16.40 C, 0.95 C above the 1991-2020 average and 0.02 C warmer than September 2023 (+0.93 C). It was 1.76 C above pre-industrial, the second month in a row above 1.5 C. The 12-month average (October 2025 to September 2026) rose to 1.51 C above pre-industrial. Extra-polar SST set a September record of 21.08 C, well above 2023's 20.92 C, and Nino 3.4 SST reached an all-time monthly high. Western Europe had its joint-warmest September (tied with 2023), and Europe as a whole its third-warmest. NOAA and NASA also ranked the month warmest on record, though NOAA's margin over 2023 was within its stated uncertainty. NOAA reported a record ocean surface anomaly for any month.

On 15 October 2026 the CHMP reversed its earlier opinion after re-examination and recommended granting a conditional marketing authorisation for Yartemlea (EMA meeting highlights and Q&A published 16 October). The recommendation covers adults with TA-TMA. The EMA said the pivotal study had limitations, including the lack of a placebo or active comparator and patients' use of other medicines. However, the new rapporteurs found that the patient-level data submitted in August, together with the compassionate-use experience, showed response rates and survival that were consistent across analyses and unlikely to be explained by supportive care alone. The external-control survival comparison was considered supportive but not conclusive. The Ad Hoc Expert Group was consulted. It said that the high mortality of TA-TMA and the absence of any approved European treatment justified earlier access while further data were collected. Because comprehensive data were not yet available, the authorisation is conditional. Omeros must provide results from a controlled study and a European registry. The CHMP found the paediatric data too limited to support dose, efficacy or safety in children, so children were excluded from the indication pending further study. Omeros said it was "very pleased" that European patients would have access to the first approved therapy for TA-TMA. It said it would keep its EU compassionate-use programme open until commercial supply was in place, and that it expected a European Commission decision within about two months.

On 6 November 2026 the three-judge panel acquitted Lissu of treason and ordered his immediate release. It found the prosecution had failed to prove he intended to intimidate or overthrow the government. It held that his "No Reforms, No Election" slogan and remarks at the April 2025 rally were political advocacy for electoral reform, not a call to violence. Judge Ndunguru said that Section 39(2)(d), which was being interpreted for the first time, required proof of intent that the evidence of the 17 prosecution witnesses did not establish. By then Lissu had spent about 19 months in detention. He walked out of the courtroom to cheering supporters and told reporters he had been "imprisoned for an idea." He said he would continue to push for constitutional and electoral reforms ahead of the 2030 elections, and the verdict leaves him eligible to stand. The Director of Public Prosecutions said his office would study the judgment and consider an appeal to the Court of Appeal. Human Rights Watch and other groups welcomed the acquittal. They said Lissu should never have been charged and called for the release of other detained opposition members.

On 4 November 2026 Collins named "agentic" its Word of the Year 2026. Collins defines it as describing artificial intelligence systems that can act independently to carry out tasks, make decisions and pursue goals on a user's behalf, rather than simply responding to prompts. The word is formed from "agent" with the adjectival suffix "-ic". It existed for decades in psychology and philosophy, where it described a person's capacity to act on their own will. Around 2023 it was taken up in the tech industry to describe autonomous AI tools. By 2026 it was in widespread mainstream use, from corporate earnings calls to social media jokes about "agentic" fridges and kettles. The shortlist, framed as "a year of handing over the controls," was: doomscaling, rentflation, heat dome, ghost job, slopcore, deskbombing, chatbot grief, quiet cracking and P(doom).

PN replied to the RoS on 12 October. On 20 October (announced late on 19-20 October), two days before the 30-day window would have lapsed, the RoS cancelled PN's registration under subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the Societies Act. It said PN's explanation failed to refute the grounds, chiefly the exclusion of Bersatu in breach of Clause 7.1. PN considered an appeal to the home minister and said it might contest under a component party's banner. On 22 October the High Court (Judge Azizan Md Arshad) heard PN's stay application and dismissed it. He held that the deregistration was a final decision best tested at the full judicial review, and that the balance of convenience did not favour suspending it before then. The cancellation therefore remained in force, and PN could not operate or use its name and logo. On 23 October PN filed an appeal to the Court of Appeal against the refusal of the stay and sought an urgent hearing. The appellate court fixed case management for 3 November because the record of appeal was not yet complete, so no ruling came before nomination day. On 31 October PN's candidates for Melaka were nominated under the PAS logo, and Takiyuddin Hassan described the arrangement as a "temporary vehicle" for the coalition. On 4 November the Court of Appeal fixed 22 February 2027 to hear PN's appeal. The High Court set the judicial review hearing for 7 December 2026.

On Tuesday 3 November 2026 at Drouant, the Académie Goncourt awarded the 124th Prix Goncourt to Sylvain Prudhomme (47) for "De l'autre côté du lac" (Minuit). He won in the first round of voting, by six votes to three for Philippe Jaenada ("L'inconnue du quai de Javel", Flammarion). Yannick Haenel and Clémentine Mélois received no votes. Jury president Philippe Claudel said the novel "fait entendre le silence de la montagne comme une menace et comme une consolation". Prudhomme succeeds Laurent Mauvignier (2025, "La Maison vide"), and the prize returns to Éditions de Minuit for the second year running. The Prix Renaudot was announced at the same time.

The Bank of Canada held its overnight rate at 2.25% on 28 October, its eighth consecutive decision without a change (Bank Rate 2.50%, deposit rate 2.20%). Governor Tiff Macklem said the bank was "prepared to act if elevated energy prices begin to spill over and become generalized inflation," but that with core measures below 2% and the labour market softening, an immediate increase was not warranted. The guidance leaned hawkish: "Governing Council discussed whether an increase in the policy rate was needed and judged it prudent to wait for more evidence," with members stressing they would assess incoming data one meeting at a time and that a hike remained on the table.

The bank raised its inflation outlook sharply, expecting CPI around 3.4% by end-2026 and 2.9% in 2027 (from 2.0% in July), with a return to about 2% by early 2028. It trimmed its 2026 growth forecast to 0.6% (from 0.7%) and sees about 1.7% growth in 2027, citing job losses and weaker business investment. The rate remains at the low end of the bank's neutral range, below the 2.75% midpoint. The next decision is 9 December. Forecasters who called a hike, including Scotiabank, Desjardins and BMO, were wrong.

H3 Flight No. 10 did not lift off as scheduled on 20 October 2026. About two hours before the planned 04:41:03 JST liftoff, JAXA and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries halted the countdown at Tanegashima after detecting an anomaly in a ground-side pressurization system serving the second stage. The launch was postponed, continuing H3's pattern of never launching without a delay. After the equipment was inspected and replaced, the rocket lifted off at 04:36:12 JST on 24 October 2026 (19:36 UTC on 23 October) from the Yoshinobu Launch Complex, well inside the reserved period ending 9 November. JAXA reported that the rocket flew as planned. MMX separation was confirmed about 71 minutes after liftoff, and the spacecraft was injected into its predetermined orbit, a Mars transfer trajectory. Arrival at Mars is still expected in August 2027. This was H3's third consecutive success since the December 2025 Flight No. 8 failure. The Idefix rover is due to land on Phobos around the turn of 2028/2029, and sample return is planned for 2031.

On 23 October 2026, four days before its deadline, the FTC approved the acquisition subject to conditions under Article 13(2) of the Fair Trade Act. Three commissioners voted for conditional approval, one favoured blocking it, and one recused. The FTC said Uber's 13.1% stake in Grab, the long board service of Uber's CEO at Grab, and the two companies' past cooperation, including Grab's 2018 takeover of Uber's Southeast Asia business, did create a risk of weakened competition in a highly concentrated market with high barriers to entry. But it found that this risk could be addressed through binding remedies. It also noted that keeping foodpanda as an independent competitor to Uber Eats was preferable to the business weakening.

The conditions largely followed Grab's offer. Grab must dilute Uber's stake, bar Uber representatives and nominees from its board and committees, and set up an information firewall preventing any exchange of Taiwan pricing, commission or rider data with Uber. Grab must also keep Taiwan user data stored outside mainland China, refrain from raising merchant commissions above set levels for three years, and submit annual compliance reports to the FTC. The FTC said it could revoke approval or impose fines if the conditions were breached.

Grab said it "welcomed" the decision and would work to strengthen foodpanda in its first market outside Southeast Asia. Delivery Hero said it expected the deal to close by year-end. Delivery-worker unions and the New Power Party criticised the ruling, saying the conditions could not be reliably enforced.

Isaias made landfall near Pensacola Beach, Florida (30.3N 87.1W, about 8 miles south of Pensacola) at about 7:45 PM CDT on 9 October 2026 (0045 UTC 10 October). This was its first and only US landfall. NHC, using Hurricane Hunter and NWS Doppler radar data, gave maximum sustained winds of 115 mph (185 km/h), a Category 3 major hurricane, and an estimated minimum central pressure of 964 mb. Earlier that day it had peaked with 120 mph winds and 959 mb, and it weakened only slightly as it came ashore. Reported gusts reached 124 mph near Gulf Breeze, with sustained winds of 97 mph there, and 108 mph at Pensacola. Water levels reached about 6.8 ft above MHHW at Pensacola Bay. Isaias weakened rapidly inland and became post-tropical over Alabama by 10 October. Five people died. Outages peaked at about 1.05 million customers across eight states, including about 512,000 in Florida and 389,000 in Alabama, and about 790,000 were still without power at midday on 10 October. Pensacola's airport was damaged and closed to commercial flights.

Jodi failed to sell on 27 October 2026. Bidding stalled at US$5.2 million, below the US$6 million low estimate, and the auctioneer passed the lot after about four minutes. Only two bidders took part, one in the room and one on the telephone, and neither went beyond the opening rounds. It was the first high-profile dinosaur skeleton to go unsold at a major auction house since the market's recent run of record prices, which included "Gus" the T. rex (US$50.1 million, Sotheby's, July 2026) and "Apex" the Stegosaurus (US$44.6 million). Sotheby's said it would explore a private sale. The consignor had not been identified by 28 October. The result renewed debate over whether a Nanotyrannus can command T. rex-level prices, and over the wisdom of offering scientifically important fossils on the open market.

Bukele pulled back rather than escalating. On 21 October he suspended El Salvador's participation in the Gang Suppression Force. On X he accused the force's backers of leaving his men "alone in the field" and said Salvadoran crews would not fly further missions until their safety could be guaranteed. On 22 October the contingent's helicopters were grounded at their base near Port-au-Prince, and the next day a Salvadoran air force transport flew home non-essential personnel and some equipment. On 28 October, after a phone call between Bukele and Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, El Salvador's foreign ministry announced that the "Liberty II" contingent would be withdrawn from Haiti. A small team would stay behind to coordinate the search for the four men with Haitian police and the GSF. The statement said El Salvador remained "committed to the Haitian people" but would not keep troops in a mission that lacked "the resources and the rules to win." It was unclear whether the country would ever rejoin the force. Earlier that week Haiti had handed over four bodies said to be the missing men, but Salvadoran officials rejected them: one was a child and another wore a different country's uniform. On 2 November Haitian police and GSF troops from other contingents began an operation in the Plain of the Cul-de-Sac, with no Salvadoran soldiers taking part. By early November the burned vehicle had been found but there was no sign of the four men. The same week Haiti postponed its elections to 2027.

The launch was a solid success, though it fell well short of Black Myth: Wukong and below some of the pre-launch hype. Steam concurrent players peaked at 389,412 within 24 hours of the 29 October launch (SteamDB). Over the weekend the peak rose to 411,857 on Sunday 1 November. That made it Steam's second-biggest launch of 2026, behind Wardogs (428,666) but ahead of Resident Evil Requiem (344,214) and Forza Horizon 6 (302,645). It ranked fifth among all Steam games at the time, behind Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, PUBG and Banana. On 2 November S-Game announced more than 2.3 million copies sold in the first 72 hours across PS5, Steam, Epic and WeGame, all digital. That was a little under a quarter of Wukong's 10 million in three days. Critics' reception held up at 88 on Metacritic, which was called the highest-rated Chinese game ever. User reception was more divided, largely because of PC performance problems, including stuttering and shader-compilation hitches on mid-range hardware. Steam user reviews settled at "Mostly Positive", with 74-77% positive. Metacritic user scores were 71 on PC and 86 on PS5. S-Game said a performance patch was in progress.

On 4 November 2026 NASA and NOAA reported that the 2026 ozone hole was the 13th-largest in 48 years of monitoring by seasonal mean area. From 7 September to 13 October it averaged about 22.4 million km2 (8.6 million square miles). Its largest single-day extent was 26.6 million km2 (10.3 million square miles) on 21 September, about 88% of the record set on 9 September 2000. NASA's Paul Newman said the hole grew rapidly in September because of a cold, strong polar vortex. It then shrank faster than usual in early October after a burst of planetary-wave activity disturbed and warmed the vortex, pulling the seasonal average down. The hole was not especially deep: balloon soundings found the lowest ozone over the South Pole was 112 Dobson units on 6 October, against a record low of 92 DU in October 2006. The agencies said it would have been about 1 to 2 million square miles larger with year-2000 levels of ozone-depleting substances, that Antarctic stratospheric chlorine has fallen by about a third, and that recovery remains on track for the 2070s.

On Monday 2 November 2026, the eve of the midterms, an IRGC unit on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz fired a surface-to-air missile at a US surveillance aircraft operating over the Gulf. The missile missed, and the aircraft returned safely to base. Iranian state media (IRNA) said that air-defence units had "warned off" an intruding American aircraft. US officials confirmed the incident but said no American forces had fired on Iranian territory in response. They described the US posture as "restraint consistent with the president's commitment" and said commanders had been instructed to avoid actions that could unravel the ceasefire before the vote. The Wall Street Journal reported that this was the latest in a series of similar IRGC provocations in recent weeks, including drone approaches toward US warships that were intercepted over open water. NBC was told the Pentagon had prepared response options for such incidents but that none had been authorised before 3 November. No US strike on Iran was reported through Election Day, and the Polymarket "ceasefire continues through the midterms" market resolved Yes. Afterwards, diplomacy via Qatar continued. By 7 November a Qatari plan was reported that would have the US lift the naval blockade and release some frozen assets, in exchange for IAEA inspections and Iran reopening the strait. Meanwhile Netanyahu was reported to be pressing Trump for renewed military action, and US officials said strike options remained under review now that the elections had passed.

Paxton won comfortably, far more decisively than polls suggested. Texas Secretary of State results (100% of polling locations): Ken Paxton (R) 5,138,416 votes (~52.0%), James Talarico (D) 4,553,207 (~46.1%), Libertarian Ted Brown 186,904. The AP called the race late on election night once returns from the suburban counties around Houston and Dallas came in short of Democratic targets. Paxton held the seat for Republicans, extending the Democrats' drought in Texas statewide races past 30 years. The roughly 6-point margin defied both the final polls, which ranged from a tie to Talarico +5, and Kalshi's margin forecast of about Talarico +2. Record early turnout had not translated into the Democratic edge many analysts expected, as heavy Election Day voting in rural and exurban counties favoured Paxton. The result ran against the national trend: Democrats won control of the House amid a broad anti-Trump mood, but fell short of a Senate majority after gains in North Carolina and Maine. Texas was the most closely watched Republican hold of the night and a vindication for Trump, Abbott and Cruz, who had campaigned repeatedly for Paxton in the final weeks.

GLP-1. On 5 October 2026 the Nobel Assembly awarded the prize jointly to Daniel Drucker (Lunenfeld-Tanenbaum Research Institute and University of Toronto, Canada, 70), Jens Juul Holst (University of Copenhagen, Denmark, 81) and Svetlana Mojsov (Rockefeller University, USA, 79) "for their discoveries concerning the incretin hormone glucagon-like peptide-1". Each receives a third of SEK 12 million. Mojsov identified and synthesised the active form of GLP-1 in the intestine in the 1980s. Holst showed that the shortened peptide powerfully stimulated insulin release. Drucker demonstrated its action on insulin-producing cells and went on to map its wider effects on metabolism. The long-tipped optogenetics researchers missed out again. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen of Novo Nordisk, whose work led to the long-acting drugs liraglutide and semaglutide, was left out, while Mojsov, whose early contribution had long been overlooked, was included. Clarivate noted that all three laureates had been named among its Citation Laureates on 17 September.

On 18 October 2026 (US time; 19 October on Nikumaroro) the expedition announced that the Taraia Object was not Amelia Earhart's Electra. It was most likely a large section of steel hull plating and framing from the SS Norwich City, the British freighter wrecked on Nikumaroro's western reef in 1929. Storm surges had evidently carried the debris across the reef flat and into the lagoon edge by the Taraia Peninsula. Divers and shore teams found the object half-buried in sand and partly overgrown. Its main section was a bent, roughly rectangular plate with attached ribs, which produced the wing-and-fuselage outline seen in satellite and aerial imagery. The magnetometer registered a strong anomaly over the site, consistent with a heavy mass of ferrous metal rather than the aluminium of a Lockheed Electra. Rivet patterns and plate thickness, the archaeologists said, matched early-20th-century ship construction and not aircraft manufacture. Hydroprobing nearby found further corroded steel fragments and coral rubble but no aluminium or aircraft components. Bad weather lengthened the trip, and the team spent seven days at Nikumaroro, four of them onshore. Pettigrew said the identification explained why the anomaly appeared in photographs as far back as 1938. The team said it still believed the broader castaway hypothesis and would keep studying the artefacts it recovered. Purdue pledged to continue the search.

Ueno was taken over within a week. On Tuesday 3 November the central bank placed it under special supervision, appointing an intervenor to run the bank after finding it had breached minimum solvency requirements. It stopped short of resolution, and customer accounts stayed open, although withdrawals were capped for 48 hours. The promised capital injection from Grupo Vázquez fell through. On Wednesday 4 November the central bank announced that a consortium of three domestic banks would acquire ueno's deposits and most of its loan book, backed by a state-guaranteed liquidity line of about $300 million. Central bank president Carlos Carvallo resigned on 3 November, and Peña named his deputy as interim president.

Prosecutors issued arrest warrants for five ueno executives and opened an investigation into loans to Grupo Vázquez companies. Protesters gathered outside the presidential palace demanding Peña's resignation, and opposition deputies filed an impeachment motion. On Thursday 5 November the lower house vote fell short of the two-thirds majority needed, after most Colorado deputies loyal to Peña voted against it. Several deputies from the party's rival faction backed the motion. Peña refused to resign. In a televised address he said he had cut ties with Grupo Vázquez in 2025 and would cooperate with any inquiry. On 7 November prosecutors summoned Carvallo for questioning over his recusal. Fitch downgraded ueno to 'B' and placed Paraguay's sovereign outlook under review. Ueno's 2031 bonds fell to about 55 cents on the dollar. Reuters called it Paraguay's deepest political crisis in more than a decade.

Herugavialis cairensis is an extinct gavialoid crocodylian (a gavial: a long, thin-snouted, fish-eating crocodile) that lived about 18 million years ago, in the Early Miocene (Burdigalian), in the coastal estuaries and river channels that then fringed northern Egypt. It is known from a partial skull of about 20 inches, along with lower jaws and several vertebrae. These fossils were collected in the early 1900s at Wadi Moghra in the Qattara Depression, west of Cairo, from the sandstones and mudstones of the Moghra Formation. The material was described in 1907 as Gavialis sp., an unnamed relative of the living gharial of South Asia, and was then stored for most of the following century in the Egyptian Geological Museum in Cairo. CT scanning revealed differences such as unusually large, strongly raised eye-socket rims and a distinctive pattern of bones in the palate. Phylogenetic analysis showed it falls outside Gavialis and closer to the base of the gavialoid lineage, so it was given a new genus. The name honours the Egyptian god Heru (Horus), whose "Eye of Horus" (the wedjat) was a widespread protective symbol in ancient Egypt. The choice was made because the animal's prominent, upward-facing eye sockets are its most striking feature and were key to recognising it as a distinct genus. "-gavialis" reflects its kinship with Gavialis, and "cairensis" refers to Cairo, where the fossils have been held for more than a century. The paper (Burke et al.) appeared in Royal Society Open Science on 7 October 2026, with embargoed coverage published the evening of 6 October US time.

The rebel offensive stalled within days, but federal forces were unable to reverse it. Drone strikes and pro-government militias halted the Tigrayan advance in Afar in late September, and the army retook ground around Abala. In Amhara, however, Fano units pressed their attacks, briefly entering Lalibela and cutting several roads between towns in North Wollo. The Oromo Liberation Army stepped up ambushes in western and southern Oromia, forcing the federal government to keep troops away from the northern fronts. On about 2 October Ethiopia recalled its ambassador from Asmara and accused Eritrea of supplying the rebels across the border. Eritrea denied this and suspended consular services but did not cut ties. Federal counterattacks toward Tigray along the Afar and southern axes made limited progress. The TPLF kept control of Mekelle, Axum and Shire, though repeated drone strikes hit the Mekelle airport and fuel depots, and the regional government said dozens of civilians had been killed. Divisions within the TPLF surfaced publicly when some officials allied with Getachew Reda called for talks. Eritrean troops massed near the border around Zalambessa but did not cross in large numbers. Under pressure from the African Union, Olusegun Obasanjo held separate meetings with both sides in Addis Ababa and Nairobi. On 14 October the government and the TPLF agreed to a 30-day humanitarian truce on the Tigray and Afar fronts to allow aid deliveries, with talks on the Pretoria framework planned for November. Fano and the OLA rejected the truce, and fighting continued in Amhara and Oromia into mid-October.

Bombadil is a self-tending smart planter for houseplants, which Electric Plant Company called the first of its kind. It keeps a plant healthy without owner involvement by continuously measuring the plant's condition and adjusting water, light and nutrients on its own, rather than relying on fixed watering schedules or the owner noticing drooping or yellowing leaves. The planter combines a reservoir, a full-spectrum LED canopy and an array of root-zone sensors tracking moisture, temperature, salinity and oxygen. An on-board model trained on growth data from more than 20,000 houseplants across about 80 common indoor species interprets these readings, and the company says that dataset has since grown to 35,000 plants. Its first release manages six care variables, including irrigation timing, light intensity and photoperiod, and fertiliser dosing. It also adapts to species it was not specifically trained on. Plants come pre-potted from Electric Plant Company's partner greenhouses and ship inside the unit, which retails for about $249 with an optional monthly subscription for nutrient cartridges and replacement plants. Target users are apartment dwellers, offices, hotels and interior-plantscaping services, and Mast claimed plant survival rates above 95% in the first year of ownership. The company announced a $9.5M seed round led by Lerer Hippeau and Pillar VC, and opened pre-orders for delivery in early 2027.

On 24 October 2026 the United Arab Emirates announced that it had mediated a large Russia-Ukraine prisoner exchange, the first since the trilateral talks were called off. Both sides confirmed it. Ukrainian ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and his Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova, who led the humanitarian contacts, finalised the lists in an online meeting on 25 October. On 28 October each side returned 185 prisoners of war on the Belarus-Ukraine border. Ukraine said those released included defenders of Mariupol and seriously wounded soldiers. The two sides also exchanged bodies: Ukraine received about 1,000 and Russia received several dozen. Zelensky thanked the UAE and the United States and said the swap showed that "humanitarian tracks can work when Russia wants them to". The Kremlin described it as a goodwill gesture ahead of the November talks.

No ceasefire was agreed on any part of the front. Russian forces kept up assaults in the Pokrovsk and Zaporizhzhia directions. On the night of 29–30 October they launched one of the largest combined missile and drone attacks of the autumn on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, causing emergency power cuts in several regions. Ukraine struck oil refineries and fuel depots inside Russia. Ushakov said Ukraine's strikes were "not helping the atmosphere" but did not withdraw Putin's agreement to resume talks. Witkoff said technical-level trilateral talks remained planned for around 10 November, with Abu Dhabi the likely venue. The prisoner swap was the only in-person contact between the two sides during the period.

The ruling list held on to power, extending SNS rule into a fifteenth year, though without an outright majority of its own. Vučić declared victory on election night at 22:14, and Ilija Srdanović refused to concede, citing vote-buying and irregularities at hundreds of polling stations. After a repeat vote at 61 polling stations on 1 November, RIK's final results (5 November) gave "Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia" 2,071,540 votes (~47%) and 125 of 250 seats, one short of a majority. The Student List got 1,858,206 votes (~42%) and 110 seats. Dačić's SPS list narrowly cleared the threshold with about 3.4% and 8 seats. European Serbia and Authentic Right both missed it. The remaining seven seats went to minority lists: Hungarians 2, Albanian Coalition 2, SDP–CDP 1, SDA Sandžak 1, and Zukorlić's SPP 1. Turnout was 66.2%, about 7 points higher than 2023. The Student List won around two-thirds of diaspora votes. In the aftermath, Dačić announced on 7 November that SPS would again enter government with SNS, giving the coalition 133 seats. Students staged sit-ins outside RIK and RTS in Belgrade, and OSCE/ODIHR observers reported that misuse of public resources and pressure on voters had given the ruling list an unfair advantage.

The trend began with a roughly 15-20-second comedy clip that Bulin 47 posted to his own TikTok and Instagram accounts in early October 2026. One source dates the original upload to 4 October. Filmed in daylight inside a colmado in Santo Domingo, the skit showed Bulin (white tank top, gold chain, bucket hat) at the counter asking the shopkeeper how much he owed. When the shopkeeper, played by a friend, named an absurd price, Bulin froze mid-motion with a wide-eyed stare. After a beat he slowly lowered his sunglasses and said, deadpan, "¿Y eso e' pa' mí?" ("And that's for me?"), before a dembow beat dropped and he walked out backwards. The clip spread on TikTok and Instagram, and early reports cited more than 40M views across platforms. The original Instagram post was reported at 55M to 80M+ views.

It then became a reaction-meme format. People first used the audio to lip-sync, then filmed themselves receiving bad news, such as a high restaurant bill, an exam grade, a breakup text or a rent increase, and cut to their own version of the freeze, the sunglasses lowering and the backwards walk-out. Brands, sports teams and news pages followed, pairing the audio with fan reactions to transfer fees, ticket prices and election results. Football clubs posted players "reacting" to refereeing decisions. A large share of entries used green-screen edits that placed Bulin's frozen face over clips of politicians, celebrities and pets. One tracker estimated about 310M views across platforms by 29 October, making it one of the month's biggest audio-based trends. Bulin 47 then released a full track built on the catchphrase, reported as "¿Y Eso E' Pa' Mí?" (10 October) or simply "Pa' Mí".

On 11 October 2026 the PTI long march, led by Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, reached the Attock bridge on the Punjab-KP border. It found the crossing and the motorway sealed with shipping containers. Islamabad and Rawalpindi were placed under Section 144, and the Interior Ministry authorised the army to deploy in the capital in aid of civil power (Article 245). Punjab police fired tear gas as marchers tried to push through. Police said 312 PTI workers were detained in Attock, Rawalpindi and Islamabad, among them MNA Junaid Akbar. Khan's three sisters were reportedly stopped outside Adiala jail.

Afridi was not arrested. After a two-day sit-in at the bridge, he announced on 13 October that the march would return to Peshawar, citing "the security of our workers". At a meeting on 12 October the federal cabinet considered, but did not approve, a proclamation of emergency or governor's rule in KP. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif repeated that it remained a "last option". Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said the matter was "deferred, not closed".

The PTI called 11 October a "black day" and on 14 October petitioned the Islamabad High Court over the detentions. National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq then brokered a resumption of government-opposition contacts. On 20 October Afridi attended a meeting of the provincial apex committee on counterterrorism with federal and military officials, the first in months, and agreed to a joint review of operations in the southern districts. He told the assembly the next day that the province had "not surrendered its consent". The PTI government remained in office, with Afridi as chief minister, through the end of October.

Flávio Bolsonaro won the runoff, holding on to his first-round lead. With 100% of ballots counted, the TSE reported Flávio 51.20% (63,530,124 votes) to Lula's 48.80% (60,552,149), a margin of about 2.98 million votes (2.4 points). Turnout was about 80.6%, only slightly above the first round, despite the Lula campaign's push to mobilise abstainers. The result kept intact the pattern since 1985 that no candidate has won the presidency after trailing in the first round. It also made Lula the second consecutive incumbent to lose a re-election bid, after Jair Bolsonaro in 2022. Flávio, 45, will take office on 1 January 2027 for a term to 2030.

The count was tense. For much of the evening Lula led, buoyed by early returns from the Northeast, before Flávio overtook him as votes from São Paulo, Paraná and Santa Catarina came in. Lula did not speak publicly for several hours. Some PT figures questioned results in individual states and called for audits. TSE president Kássio Nunes Marques confirmed Flávio's victory that night. Lula recognised the result the following day and pledged an orderly transition. In his victory speech, Flávio thanked his father and repeated his campaign promise to seek amnesty for those convicted over 8 January 2023, which revived debate over a possible pardon for Jair Bolsonaro. World leaders, including U.S. President Donald Trump and Argentina's Javier Milei, congratulated Flávio.

The outcome vindicated prediction markets, which had given Flávio roughly 75-80% until election day. Final-week polls, which had shown a statistical tie, underestimated his margin.

The offensive came after a delay of nearly two weeks and was narrow. On 14-15 October Presidential Leadership Council chair Rashad al-Alimi announced "Operation Golden Strait" from Aden. It aimed to restore government control of the Bab al-Mandab coast and islands, and it explicitly did not target Sanaa. Saudi officials described its air component as "intensive but limited in scope". The same day, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan announced that additional Pakistani air defence units would deploy to the kingdom's western coast. Advancing from the south, government forces led by the Giants Brigades, with Tihama Resistance units, retook Dhubab and its airfield on 16 October. The Houthis initially denied the losses.

The Houthis hit back with missiles and drones on Jeddah, Yanbu and Aramco facilities on the Red Sea coast. A 19 October strike on a Yanbu loading terminal killed 7 people and halted exports there for about five days. Fighting around Mocha lasted more than a week. On 24 October government sources said the town centre and port were under their control, though Houthi units still held positions to the north and east. Perim (Mayun) Island was retaken on 28 October after a landing supported by Saudi helicopters. Houthi media acknowledged a "tactical repositioning" from the island. The Hanish islands remained contested.

By 5 November analysts described the strait as back under nominal government control, with Saudi-linked tanker traffic resuming cautiously under naval escort and oil prices easing slightly. The government claimed heavy Houthi losses (about 4,800 killed or wounded). The Houthis stepped up attacks in Taiz and Al-Bayda, where fronts were largely unchanged. They also kept up their "maritime embargo", firing at two tankers in the southern Red Sea without sinking either. No ceasefire was agreed. Omani officials said that indirect contacts between Riyadh and the Houthis had resumed, and Saudi officials did not deny this.

Merab Dvalishvili regained the bantamweight title by unanimous decision, 48-47 on all three scorecards, in what was called a Fight of the Year contender. Yan clearly won the first two rounds on all three cards and the first half of the third, stuffing early takedowns and landing to the body. A Dvalishvili takedown midway through round 3 turned the fight, and from then on it was entirely Dvalishvili's: he took rounds 3, 4 and 5 on every card, chaining takedowns and outworking Yan against the fence. Dvalishvili said his coach told him going into the fifth that it was 2-2 and whoever won the round would win the fight. It was the 20th trilogy in UFC history, and Dvalishvili won the series 2-1. In the main event, Alexander Volkanovski retained the featherweight title with a second-round TKO of the previously unbeaten Movsar Evloev.

The reissue sent The Black Parade back to No. 2 in both countries, matching its 2006 peak but again stopping one place short of the band's first No. 1 album. UK (Official Albums Chart, announced 30 Oct 2026): it climbed 162-2 with 16,840 units, up 1,112% on the week (6,402 CDs, 7,731 vinyl, 804 cassettes, 311 downloads, 1,592 sales-equivalent streams). Fontaines D.C.'s Dopamine Chamber held at No. 1 for a second week with 18,215 units. Olivia Rodrigo was No. 3, and the reissue of Amy Winehouse's 20-year-old Back to Black re-entered at No. 4. The Official Charts Company said the race had been close all week, with the two albums swapping the lead on midweek updates. In 2006 the album's 85,805 first-week UK sales had lost No. 1 to Robbie Williams' Rudebox. US (Billboard 200 dated 7 Nov, announced 1 Nov 2026): it jumped 139-2 with 61,000 equivalent album units, up 489%. Pure sales were 52,000, up 1,571%, of which 33,000 were vinyl (the band's best vinyl week ever), plus 9,000 streaming units (9.31m streams). Rodrigo's you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love stayed at No. 1 with 64,000 units, down 15% as the Chappell Roan remix boost faded. Billboard noted the 139-2 climb was the album's highest-charting week since its original release and the biggest leap into the top two by an anniversary reissue in years, with pure sales topping the chart. Variety reported that some signed and store-exclusive vinyl variants had shipped late and would count the following week. In 2006 it had been held at No. 2 in the US by the Hannah Montana soundtrack.

MOIO met its primary endpoint. Enrolment was completed in February 2026, with 627 of a planned 646 patients randomised (March 2022 to February 2026) at 41 French centres. In the modified intention-to-treat population (598 patients, median follow-up 20.4 months), median PFS was 24.1 months with standard dosing versus 23.6 months with 12-weekly dosing (HR 1.04, 95% CI roughly 0.84-1.28). Because the upper bound of the confidence interval fell below the non-inferiority margin of 1.30, non-inferiority was shown. Overall survival was similar: deaths were 12.8% with reduced-frequency dosing versus 13.4% with standard dosing (OS HR about 0.97, p=0.86).

Toxicity fell modestly. Grade 3-4 immune-related adverse events were 7.1% versus 11.3%, and serious adverse events 21.4% versus 26.0%. Patients in the 12-weekly arm made roughly a third as many infusion visits, and a preliminary cost analysis suggested substantial savings in drug spending. Subgroup results were broadly consistent across lung, kidney, urothelial and head and neck cancer. Confidence intervals were wide in melanoma and the smaller tumour types, so those findings are hypothesis-generating only.

A pharmacokinetic sub-study found that trough drug levels stayed above the presumed receptor-saturating threshold in most patients at 12 weeks. Gravis said 12-weekly dosing is a reasonable option for patients responding at six months and could reduce burden on patients and hospitals. She added that longer follow-up is needed to confirm the durability of the result.

Barcelona beat Real Madrid 2-1 at the Spotify Camp Nou (attendance 62,055), completing a 100% start of ten straight league wins and stretching their lead at the top to nine points. Raphinha scored both Barcelona goals. Madrid went ahead in the 34th minute when Kylian Mbappe ran onto Arda Guler's through ball and finished low past Joan Garcia. Barcelona equalised in the 52nd minute when Raphinha met Lamine Yamal's cross at the far post with a volley that Andriy Lunin could not keep out. Joan Garcia then made a big save from a Jude Bellingham header, and Federico Valverde dragged a long-range shot just wide in the 74th minute. In the 86th minute, after a run from Lamine Yamal, Pedri slipped the ball through and Raphinha drove in the winner at the near post. Hansi Flick celebrated on the touchline with his staff, and players from both sides clashed at the final whistle. The referee was Juan Martinez Munuera.

Space Bunny Alpha was an anonymous ("stealth") AI model listed on OpenRouter, and also on OpenCode, from 23 September 2026. OpenRouter described it as a large model with "very fast inference, strong agentic and coding capabilities and native multimodal input support" (text and image in), adjustable reasoning effort and a 512K-token context window. It was free during the preview. On 24 September an independent tokenizer fingerprinting test matched it to Moonshot AI's Kimi models, making Moonshot the leading suspect. It was the #1 model on OpenRouter for 8 straight days and processed 41.2T tokens there, the most of any stealth model OpenRouter had run. It was delisted on 3 October without being claimed. On 14 October 2026 Moonshot AI officially launched Kimi K3 Flash and said Space Bunny had been an early version of it (over 150 trillion tokens served while anonymous). Moonshot claimed strong agentic, coding, tool-use and long-horizon research results (DeepSWE 71.9%, BrowseComp 68.4, Terminal-Bench 2 61%). Pricing was $0.20/M input and $0.80/M output, and Moonshot said the weights would be released under a modified MIT license.

Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) won from third on the grid in 2:20:31.405. It was his first win of 2026 and his second in Mexico City. He held off Max Verstappen (Red Bull) by 1.214s, with Kimi Antonelli third (+3.872s), which clinched Antonelli the 2026 world title as the youngest champion ever. Hamilton was fourth, Russell fifth and Norris sixth. On lap 1, Leclerc used the slipstream down the long run to Turn 1 and drew alongside Hamilton. The two Ferraris ran side by side through Turns 1 and 2 before Leclerc took the lead on the exit of Turn 3. Russell locked up and tagged Verstappen, who dropped to sixth before recovering. Russell received a 5s penalty. Verstappen, starting on mediums, ran long and briefly led before his stop but rejoined third. A heavy Turn 1 crash for Bottas, caused by a brake failure, brought a red flag. Leclerc led the standing restart and survived a lunge from Verstappen into Turn 1 that left both cars brushing wheels. A late Safety Car followed a Piastri-Lawson collision. Leclerc nailed the restart with seven laps left and kept Verstappen just over a second behind to the flag.

Israel's election on 27 October 2026 produced no majority for either bloc. Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar! narrowly finished first, broadly in line with the final polls. Turnout was about 75%.

**Final official results**

- Yashar!: 24 seats
- Likud: 23 seats (18.1%)
- Together (Bennett): 13
- Joint List: 11
- Democrats: 9
- Shas: 8
- Jewish Power: 8
- Yisrael Beiteinu: 8
- United Torah Judaism: 7
- Ra'am: 5
- Hendel–Zelekha Reservists: 4 (narrowly crossed the threshold)

Two lists missed the threshold:

- Religious Zionism–Zehut won 2.9%, the first time Smotrich's list had failed to enter the Knesset.
- Ofer Winter's People of Israel won 1.6%.

**The blocs**

- Netanyahu's bloc fell to 46 seats, down from 68 at its peak.
- Eisenkot's bloc won 54.
- Arab-led parties won 16.
- The Reservists list, which had declined to commit to either camp, won 4 seats and held part of the balance.

Even with the Reservists, the change bloc stood at 58, short of 61. That left it dependent on Ra'am's support or Arab parties abstaining.

**Disputes and certification**

Likud alleged that the collapse of Religious Zionism's vote had been engineered through foreign-funded campaigns and called for recounts in several polling stations. The Central Elections Committee certified the results on 4 November after finding no irregularities that changed the outcome.

**Forming a government**

President Herzog gave the first mandate to form a government to Eisenkot, with 28 days plus a possible 14-day extension. Eisenkot was backed by 63 MKs' recommendations: his bloc, the Reservists and Ra'am. Netanyahu received 46. The Joint List recommended no one.

Hopewell Rock (GB), the George Boughey-trained stayer carrying a reported A$1 million bet from owner JP McManus, won the 2026 Melbourne Cup in 3:22.41 on a soft track. He was ridden by Zac Lloyd, in his first Cup, and carried 54.5kg. Sent out the $6.50 favourite after the late plunge, he answered questions about his stamina at his first attempt at 3200 m. Ciaron Maher's Royal Supremacy went hard for the lead and was eight lengths clear passing the 1200 m, but the field gradually reeled him in on the turn. Hopewell Rock, who had settled just behind midfield from barrier 15, was angled wide at the top of the straight, hit the front about 200 m out and held off Point Of Law by a length and a quarter. Trustyourinstinct was third for Joseph O'Brien and James McDonald, with Zahrann fourth. Point Of Law was the best of Maher's record seven runners, and topweight Sons And Lovers finished seventh. Hopewell Rock was the first favourite to win the Cup in 13 years and gave Boughey his first Melbourne Cup. He was also the first British-trained winner since Cross Counter in 2018.

Benson Kipruto successfully defended his title in 2:06:09, becoming the first man to win back-to-back in New York since 2013 and claiming his fifth World Marathon Major. A large lead pack passed 10 km in 30:49 and halfway in 1:03:58. Zouhair Talbi made repeated surges, including on the Queensboro Bridge after 25 km, but each was covered. Kipruto's 4:37 23rd mile on Fifth Avenue cut the group to four men: Kipruto, Andreas Almgren, Yemaneberhan Crippa and Deresa Geleta. Almgren, on his marathon debut, led narrowly at 40 km but began to labour as the course climbed into Central Park. Geleta was dropped first, then Almgren. Kipruto pulled away from Crippa inside the final mile to win by 9 seconds (Crippa 2:06:18). Almgren held on for third in 2:06:31, ahead of Geleta in 2:06:40, finishing as the fastest debutant in the race's history.

At the roughly 30-minute event in McGregor, Texas, the Roadster made three live runs on a closed strip in front of spectators held well back from the track. A standard electric launch was timed at 1.74 seconds from 0 to 60 mph. With the cold-gas thruster system developed with SpaceX engaged, a second run was timed at 1.19 seconds (Tesla said 1.06 s with rollout subtracted). In a final demo, the thrusters lifted the car off a short ramp for a brief hop that landed it about 40 feet down the track. Onboard footage showed it airborne for well under a second. Tesla announced two configurations: a standard Roadster at $200,000, which it said was road-legal, and a "SpaceX Package" with rear thrusters and a composite pressure tank. Tesla said the package was pending regulatory review for street use and priced it at $250,000 including a Founders Series reservation. It claimed a top speed of 250+ mph and 600+ miles of range, and Musk said deliveries would begin in late 2027. Reporters said the acceleration was impressive but fell well short of the "flying car" hype. Polymarket's "0-60 under 1 second" and "flies for 1s+" markets both resolved No.

The Tampa Bay Rays won the 2026 World Series 4-2, clinching their first championship in franchise history with a 5-2 win in Game 6 at American Family Field on 30 October.

- **Game 1:** Brewers 4-1. Jacob Misiorowski struck out 10 over seven innings, and his fastball touched 103 mph in the first.
- **Game 2:** Rays 6-3. Junior Caminero hit a three-run home run in the sixth off Logan Henderson, ending the Brewers' eight-game postseason winning streak.
- **Game 3:** Rays 3-2 in 10 innings. Yandy Diaz hit a walk-off double into the left-field corner after Christian Yelich's ninth-inning home run had tied the game.
- **Game 4:** Brewers 7-2. Jackson Chourio homered twice, and Milwaukee scored five runs in the third inning.
- **Game 5:** Rays 4-1. Freddy Peralta allowed one run over six and two-thirds innings against his former team.
- **Game 6:** Rays 5-2. Drew Rasmussen held Milwaukee to one run over five innings, Caminero drove in two runs off Misiorowski in the fourth, and the Tampa Bay bullpen retired the final nine batters.

Caminero was named World Series MVP after hitting .375 with three home runs and eight RBIs. Peralta won two games in the series, giving him four wins for the postseason. Tampa Bay went 9-for-12 on automated ball-strike (ABS) challenges. William Contreras hit .350 for Milwaukee in a losing effort. The Brewers, who had won seven of eight playoff games before the World Series, finished the postseason 9-4.
